description:
FOUND s470bx (Opus, resume) while probing #1237, PRE-EXISTING at fcf076f1 and
independent of it.  A `<...>` GLOB whose interpolation yields THREE OR MORE
pieces emits an N-ARY call to the BINARY `p-.`, and the whole program dies at
LOAD.

REPRO (scratch/s470bx/pglob3.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs PCL:

    my $h = "passwd";
    my @a = <a${h}b>;    # perl 1   PCL dies
    my @b = </etc/${h}>; # perl 1   PCL 1     (TWO pieces -- fine)
    my @c = </etc/$h*>;  # perl 2   PCL dies  (an ordinary spelling)

Emission (`./pl2cl`):

    (p-array-= @a (p-list-ctx (p-glob (p-. "a" $h "b"))))      ; 3 args
    (p-array-= @b (p-list-ctx (p-glob (p-. "/etc/" $h))))      ; 2 args, OK
    (p-array-= @c (p-list-ctx (p-glob (p-. "/etc/" $h "*"))))  ; 3 args

`cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:4366` is `(defun p-. (a b) ...)` -- BINARY.  The failure
is therefore not a wrong value but a dead file:

    Unhandled sb-int:simple-program-error: invalid number of arguments: 3
    0: (P-. "a" "passwd" "*") [external]

i.e. the #138 family's louder cousin: nothing is dropped, but the emitted form
cannot be called and the program never starts.  It reproduces on a `git
archive fcf076f1` extraction, so it is not #1043/#1231/#1237.

WHERE: whoever builds the `p-glob` argument from the angle-bracket contents
concatenates the interpolation pieces with a fold that assumes `p-.` is
n-ary.  Every other interpolation site in the compiler goes through
`p-string-concat` (n-ary, and overload-aware since #402/#119) -- rule 11 says
this site should reach the SAME helper rather than grow an arity fix of its
own.  Note the two-piece case works, which is why the bug survived: the common
`<$dir/*>` spelling is exactly two.

SIZE: an emission change (generation bump + the three artifacts + corpus-diff
+ emission-ab), so it is not a filler inside a runtime-only session.

RELATED: #488 (brace expansion is missing, so `glob("{$h}")` answers 0 where
perl answers 1) is a DIFFERENT gap in the same construct and stays open; the
`<{$h}>` spelling hits BOTH.
